title: Brace a crate in its bay with the one dunnage block that fits the gap
instruction: The crate can slide in its bay. Fill the gap between the crate and the near wall of the bay with the one wooden block that fits it closely, so the crate can slide no more than 3 mm.
context: Freight handlers block and brace cargo so it cannot shift in transit, filling the void between a load and a bulkhead with dunnage that fits. Here the robot must judge a 62 mm gap by eye and pick, from four blocks 6 to 10 mm apart in thickness, the one that fills it. Unlike picking a pin that fits a hole, a block that is too thin still drops into the gap and looks done, but leaves the crate free to slide, which scores as a half failure.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Load bay (fixed, light-grey painted wood): four walls 10 mm thick and 40 mm tall standing on the table, enclosing a floor (the table) 262.5 mm front to back and 162 mm side to side, centred 30.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 11.0 cm left of the midline. The near wall's inside face is 16.875 cm in front of the arm bases, the far wall's 43.125 cm; the side walls' inside faces are 2.9 and 19.1 cm left of the midline, and the side walls are 282.5 mm long. Crate (loose): a closed wooden box 200 mm front to back, 160 mm side to side and 50 mm tall, 800 g, standing on the bay floor centred side to side (1 mm from each side wall) with its far face 0.5 mm from the far wall, so its near face is 23.075 cm in front of the arm bases and the empty gap between it and the near wall is 62.0 mm. Dunnage blocks (loose, unfinished pine, all the same colour): four rectangular blocks, each 70 mm side to side and 75 mm tall, standing upright in a row 30.0 cm left of the midline with their thickness front to back. From nearest the robot: 54 mm thick (128 g) centred 16.0 cm in front of the arm bases; 66 mm thick (156 g) at 24.0 cm; 60 mm thick (142 g) at 32.0 cm; 44 mm thick (104 g) at 40.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged on the end state, with a ruler or feeler gauge. Play is how far the crate can slide front to back in the bay: the bay's inside length (262.5 mm) minus the crate's length (200 mm) minus the thickness of every block that counts (equivalently, the sum of the open gaps along the bay). Each block's own thickness is used (44, 54, 60 or 66 mm), so a block that is turned slightly is credited with its thickness, not with the wider space it spans diagonally. A block counts when all of these hold: its bottom is within 1.5 mm of the bay floor; it lies inside the bay's walls (1 mm of overlap with a wall allowed, for contact); its thickness runs front to back, within 5 degrees of parallel to the bay's long walls; it is not leaning (one of its edges within 3 degrees of vertical), so it may stand on its 70 mm wide end or lie on its 75 mm face, which leaves its thickness front to back either way; it is entirely in front of or behind the crate (at most 1 mm of overlap with the crate front to back); and it is at rest. A block that leans more than 3 degrees, is turned more than 5 degrees, rests on the crate or a wall top, or is still moving adds nothing. A block standing on the floor counts whether or not a gripper still touches it, since the floor holds it either way. At rest means moving less than 1 cm/s and turning less than 0.5 rad/s. The crate must stand on the bay floor (bottom within 1.5 mm of it), inside the walls (1 mm overlap allowed), with its 200 mm length within 5 degrees of parallel to the bay's long walls and an edge within 3 degrees of vertical, at rest; otherwise the score is 0. Score 1.0: play of at most 3 mm (only the 60 mm block in the gap gives this: 2.5 mm). Score 0.5: play of more than 3 mm and at most 10 mm (the 54 mm block in the gap: 8.5 mm). Score 0 in every other case: the 44 mm block alone (18.5 mm of play), no block in the gap, a block that does not count, or the crate off the floor, tilted, turned or moving. A block may be put in the gap on either side of the crate; if the crate is pushed toward the near wall, the gap opens at the far wall and a block there counts the same. The 66 mm block cannot enter the gap, a block turned with its 70 or 75 mm side front to back cannot either, and no two blocks fit in it together. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step.
reset_notes: Push the crate back against the far wall, centred side to side, and stand the four blocks back in their row, nearest to farthest 54, 66, 60 and 44 mm thick. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes with the simulator's default friction; masses are computed from pine at 450 kg/m3 and an 800 g crate, not measured. The bay walls are fixed and do not flex; real dunnage is often cut or wedged to fit and can be compressed, which rigid blocks cannot. The blocks carry no thickness markings, so the choice is made by eye. With 1 mm side clearance only front-to-back play is scored. Restraint is judged by the free gap, not by a load or vibration test.
